title: Rulemaking and adjudication
question: When must an agency make policy by rule, and how much procedure is required?

steps.note: Agencies may choose between rulemaking and adjudication.
A purely prospective rule announced in adjudication is not a valid rule.
Formal rulemaking only when the statute says “on the record after opportunity for a hearing”.
The choice of adjudication over rulemaking is largely the agency’s.
Notice must disclose the data the agency relies on; concise statement must answer major comments.
Courts cannot impose procedures beyond the APA.
Interpretive rules need no notice and comment, even when they change.
